documents.title: Prenatal Update (received)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OB/MFM prenatal note 1/6/2025, faxed for PCP records.

33w0d DCDA twins. Gestational diabetes controlled on diet. Growth concordant. Feels well; no breathlessness at rest, no orthopnea, no swelling beyond mild ankle puffiness of pregnancy. Carvedilol, sertraline, prenatal vitamin.

RSV vaccine (Abrysvo) given today at 33 weeks for infant protection.
Plan: delivery planning at 37-38 weeks per twin protocol; anesthesia consult given cardiac history; latex-free precautions on L&D.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

documents.title: Leave Form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! OB filled out the leave paperwork for the twins this time, so you don't need to. Just wanted you to know in case HR calls. Countdown is on!

documents.title: RE: Leave Form
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know, Lily. Wishing you an easy last few weeks!

events.reason: Painless vaginal bleeding at term, twin pregnancy

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 2/6/2025, with obstetrics at bedside.

CC: vaginal bleeding, 37 weeks with twins.

HPI: 33-year-old G3P1011 at 37w3d with dichorionic diamniotic twins. About an hour before arrival she felt a sudden "pop" low in her abdomen and then began bleeding vaginally. The bleeding is not painful, has not stopped, and appears to be increasing. No fall, blow or other trauma. She feels the babies moving. Background: peripartum cardiomyopathy after her 2023 delivery with recovered function; postpartum thyroiditis in 2024. Her first child was born vaginally at term without difficulty. This pregnancy has gone smoothly apart from gestational diabetes controlled with diet, and her ultrasounds have been normal.

Meds: carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Exam: vital signs stable. Continuous fetal monitoring: both tracings reassuring. Sterile speculum: blood coming through the cervical os; vaginal walls and cervix themselves are not bleeding.

Labs: Hgb 12.2, platelets 250, PT 12 s, aPTT 30 s.

Bedside ultrasound by OB: fetal vessels running across the internal os.

Impression: vasa previa with bleeding after rupture of membranes, term twin gestation requiring delivery now.
Disposition: taken directly to the operating room by obstetrics for emergency cesarean delivery. Latex-free room. Anesthesia and cardiology notified.

events.reason: Emergency cesarean delivery, vasa previa, twins

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, #12

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital — obstetric discharge summary.
Admitted 2/6/2025, discharged 2/9/2025.

Diagnoses: dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy at 37w3d; vasa previa with bleeding; gestational diabetes, diet controlled; history of peripartum cardiomyopathy with recovered LV function.

Procedure 2/6/2025: emergency low transverse cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia, latex-free. Vasa previa confirmed at delivery. Twin A and Twin B liveborn, both vigorous; both well and roomed in with mother.

Course: uneventful. No heart failure symptoms; euvolemic on daily exams, cardiology consulted. Postpartum fingerstick checks discontinued per protocol. Breastfeeding both twins with lactation support. Incision clean and dry.

Discharge medications:
- enalapril 10 mg twice daily — RESTARTED postpartum per cardiology (compatible with breastfeeding)
- carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily
- sertraline 50 mg daily
- prenatal vitamin daily
- oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325, 1 every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, #12
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Follow-up: cardiology with echo in about 6 weeks; OB incision check 1-2 weeks and postpartum visit at 8 weeks with 75-g glucose tolerance test (history of GDM); primary care in 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Transitional Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge 2/9 after emergency c-section for vasa previa, twins both home and well. Called pt. Pain manageable, used 3 of the oxycodone tabs, now only at night. Reminded her the combo pill already has acetaminophen in it. Restarted enalapril 10 bid in hospital, no dizziness. No SOB lying flat, no leg swelling, incision dry. Nursing both, husband and her mother helping. Mood "tired but ok." PCP visit booked 2/20. Cardiology 3/17 booked.

documents.title: Office Visit — Post-Discharge
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after emergency c-section (2/6) for vasa previa at 37+3, DCDA twins both well. Here with both babies in a double stroller.

S: Recovering. Off the oxycodone since day 5. Incision a bit sore. Breathing fine, sleeps flat (when the twins let her), no swelling. Restarted enalapril 10 bid in the hospital, carvedilol 6.25 bid, sertraline 50, prenatal vitamin. Breastfeeding both, supplementing occasionally. Lots of help at home. Anxiety manageable; GAD-7 6, PHQ-9 3.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 70 kg. Heart regular, no gallop. Lungs clear. Incision low transverse, healing well, no erythema or drainage. No calf tenderness, no edema.

A/P:
1. S/p emergency cesarean — healing well. OB incision check done last week.
2. PPCM, recovered — back on enalapril; BMP today. Cardiology echo 3/17.
3. GDM in this pregnancy — OB doing the 75-g GTT at the 8-week visit; I'll see her after.
4. Postpartum thyroiditis history — TSH at the April visit.
5. Postpartum mood — screens fine, she knows to reach out early.
CBC today.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count recovered nicely after surgery, and kidney function and potassium are normal on the enalapril.

reports.text: Comparison 7/22/2024. Normal LV size and wall motion. LVEF 55%. Normal RV size and function. Valves structurally normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 55%, normal wall motion; no change.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology 3/17/2025, about 6 weeks after cesarean delivery of twins.

No recurrence: she is without dyspnea, orthopnea or edema. Exam euvolemic.
Echo: LVEF 55%, normal wall motion.

PPCM with sustained recovery through a subsequent (twin) pregnancy.
Plan: continue enalapril 10 mg BID and carvedilol 6.25 mg BID. Echo in a year. Any future pregnancy — stop enalapril at the positive test and let us know.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

documents.title: Obstetrics Postpartum Visit (received)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN — postpartum visit 4/3/2025, 8 weeks after cesarean delivery of twins (vasa previa).

She feels well overall. She has noticed she is thirstier than usual and urinating more often. Breastfeeding the twins. Gestational diabetes in this pregnancy was managed with diet alone. History of peripartum cardiomyopathy (recovered) and postpartum thyroiditis. No headaches, visual changes or abdominal pain.

Meds: enalapril 10 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Exam: vital signs normal. Incision well healed. Abdomen and pelvic exam unremarkable.

75-g oral glucose tolerance test this morning: fasting 88 mg/dL, 1 hour 184 mg/dL, 2 hours 158 mg/dL. By nonpregnant criteria the fasting value is normal and the 2-hour value falls in the impaired glucose tolerance range.

Assessment: postpartum, recovering well; impaired glucose tolerance after gestational diabetes.
Plan: forwarded to PCP for long-term follow-up and prevention of type 2 diabetes. Annual glucose screening going forward.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit — Glucose Tolerance
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the OB's glucose tolerance test.

S: OGTT 4/3: fasting 88, 1 h 184, 2 h 158 — 2-hour value in the IGT range. She had diet-controlled GDM with the twins and her mother has type 2 diabetes. Still thirsty and peeing more than she used to, though she is nursing twins and drinking a lot of water. No weight loss, no vision change. Breastfeeding most feeds.

Meds: enalapril 10 bid, carvedilol 6.25 bid, sertraline 50, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 67 kg (pre-pregnancy ~60).

A/P:
1. Impaired glucose tolerance after GDM, family history of T2DM. A1c and UA today.
   - Discussed lifestyle (she walks the twins daily; working on portions) and metformin — in women with prior GDM it lowers progression to diabetes, and it is fine with breastfeeding. She'd like to start.
   - Metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals. GI side effects reviewed; take with food.
   - A1c again in about 6 months, or yearly.
2. Thirst/urination — UA today; likely nursing-related, but checking.
3. Postpartum thyroiditis history — TSH today.
4. PPCM — stable per cardiology.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lily — A1c 5.9%, which is in the prediabetes range and fits the glucose test. No sugar in the urine and the urinalysis is otherwise normal. Thyroid normal. Keep going with the metformin and the walks; we'll recheck in the fall.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thanks. Stomach was a little off the first two days with metformin but better now.

documents.title: Metformin 90-Day Supply
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy requesting metformin 500 mg #180 (90 days) per insurance preference. Pt tolerating per last message. Pended.

PCP: sent, 3 refills.

documents.title: Pregnant Again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So... positive test again. LMP 6/9. Stopped the enalapril like last time, didn't take it last night or this morning. What about the metformin?

documents.title: Pregnancy — Medication Plan
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spoke with pt. About 5 weeks by LMP 6/9/25.
- Enalapril stopped (last dose 7/13 AM). Off med list.
- Metformin: discussed with her OB's office this morning — they will do early glucose testing given her GDM history and prefer she stop metformin now and let testing guide treatment. Stopped.
- Continue carvedilol 6.25 bid, sertraline 50, prenatal vitamin.
- Messaged cardiology; they will see her with an echo.
She sounds steady. She knows the warning symptoms.

reports.text: Comparison 3/17/2025. Normal LV size, normal wall motion, LVEF 55%. Normal RV. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Cardio-Obstetrics Consultation (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology 8/11/2025. 34-year-old, 9 weeks pregnant (fourth pregnancy), PPCM 2023 with recovered EF, uneventful twin pregnancy with cesarean 2/2025.

Asymptomatic. Echo: LVEF 55%, unchanged.

Plan: continue carvedilol through pregnancy; no ACE inhibitor until delivery; echo each trimester and postpartum with MFM; restart enalapril after delivery. Allergies: sulfa, latex.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34F annual. 11 weeks pregnant (LMP 6/9/25), fourth pregnancy; twins are 6 months and her oldest is almost 2. OB, MFM and cardiology involved. Echo 8/11 EF 55%.

Interval: tired, some nausea, otherwise well. No breathlessness, orthopnea, palpitations or swelling. Enalapril and metformin stopped 7/14. On carvedilol 6.25 bid, sertraline 50, prenatal vitamin. Stopped nursing the twins this summer.

Allergies: sulfa, latex. FH/SH unchanged — teacher, back to school next week; never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight 66 kg. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, well-healed low transverse incision. No edema. GAD-7 5, PHQ-9 4.

A/P:
- IGT — off metformin in pregnancy; OB doing early and 24-28 week glucose testing.
- PPCM recovered — per cardiology, carvedilol continued.
- Postpartum thyroiditis history — TSH today; recheck after delivery.
- GAD — stable on sertraline.
- Flu and COVID in October. Tdap with OB. Pap after delivery.
- CBC, TSH today.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count and thyroid normal. Good luck with the first week of school!

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 17 weeks pregnant. Flu (trivalent) IM L deltoid, 2025-26 COVID IM R deltoid, latex-free. Tolerated, VIS given. Sent copy to OB.

documents.title: Sertraline Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can you send the sertraline to the pharmacy? They said it needs a new prescription. Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Sertraline Refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent — sertraline 50 mg, 90 days with refills.
